newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain's Alba invests $26 mln on fume treatment.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain's Alba invests $26 mln on fume treatment.

text.p: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) said on Sunday it had spent $26 million on two fume treatment plants to provide further environmental protection at its smelter.

"We believe that our environmental protection programme is one of the most stringent among smelters throughout the world," general manager for carbon and metal services Jaffer Amiri said in the statement.
Alba, the Middle East's biggest aluminium producer, has spent more than $250 million on advanced technology to improve the environment.

It said in May that work had started on a $23.6 million shipping terminal to handle liquid pitch in line with the company's plans to switch to more environmentally-friendly liquid form of the raw material.
The Bahraini government holds a 77 percent stake in Alba and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund 20 percent. German group Breton Investments holds the rest.
